trigger.finding: The frozen G1 concentration statistic has high power against strong species-specific spatial boundaries even when shared_species_fraction=0, because the within-species colour-permutation null removes species-specific spatial colour structure as well as cross-species alignment.

interpretive_partition.G1_concentration_test: Evidence about aggregate spatial organization/concentration of within-species flower-colour discontinuity relative to a null with no within-species colour-geography association. G1 alone is not an identifiable test of shared absolute global boundary coordinates.
interpretive_partition.species_disjoint_commonness_test: Required existing test for whether discontinuity locations learned from one species subset predict absolute global coordinates for independent species.

allowed_for_G1_alone: aggregate spatial concentration of within-species flower-colour discontinuity
directional excess spatial organization relative to within-species colour permutation
language_rules.common_coordinate_claim_requires: independent species-disjoint or another structure-preserving alignment test

future_direct_alignment_extension.question: Do species-specific discontinuity fields align in absolute geography more than expected when each species' internal spatial colour structure is preserved?
future_direct_alignment_extension.preferred_null_principle: preserve each species' internal colour-geography structure, sampling geometry, edge ranks and field shape while randomizing its absolute placement/alignment independently of other species
future_direct_alignment_extension.warning: Any concrete rotation/translation scheme must be frozen before its observed alignment statistic is computed and must not be chosen from favourable observed locations.

claim_ceiling: The combined evidence may distinguish aggregate within-species spatial organization from common cross-species geographic coordinates. This amendment changes interpretation precision, not any frozen support decision.
